solution: Infection moves exactly two edges at a time, so the set a compromised host reaches is the set of vertices joined to it by an even-length walk. In a connected graph that set is everything iff the graph has an odd cycle; if the component is bipartite the infection never leaves the starting host's colour class. So one host can infect all N iff the whole graph is connected and non-bipartite. Let k be the number of connected components, counting isolated vertices: joining components in a tree with k-1 edges preserves bipartiteness, so the answer is k-1 when some component already contains an odd cycle and k otherwise (the extra edge is added inside one colour class, always possible since N>=3). One DFS/BFS pass that 2-colours every component computes both facts in O(N+M) for N,M up to 5*10^5.
statement_summary: In an undirected network of up to five hundred thousand hosts and links, an infected host infects every host lying exactly two links away, and each newly infected host then spreads the same way. The task is to report the minimum number of additional links that must be installed so that compromising one suitably chosen host eventually infects every host in the network.
notes: The whole problem is 'count components, test bipartiteness, answer k-1 or k'; the hop-two-at-a-time rule is a disguise for even-length walks. parity-argument is the weakest of the three labels -- it names the same insight bipartite-graph does -- but the even-walk parity step is the actual deduction and is a query people make, so it is kept at lower confidence. Did NOT label dfs/bfs or union-find: the traversal is scaffolding for the 2-colouring, and graph-modeling does not apply since the graph is given. verify_hoppers.py brute-forces the true answer (try every set of added non-edges by size, simulate the two-hop closure from every start vertex) and agrees with the formula on all 872 graphs on 3 and 4 vertices exhaustively plus 800 random graphs on 5 and 6 vertices, and on samples 1 and 2; sample 3 (N=12) is checked against the formula only.
